evidence_items.heading: Comment on #12435 by @DresdenGman
evidence_items.text:
[pydantic/pydantic #12435 Comment by @DresdenGman]

I’d like to work on this. Could I be assigned to the issue?

I reviewed the existing third-party workflow and the current upstream test setups. My proposed implementation is two independent, Linux-based jobs that follow the workflow’s existing pattern:

- check out each upstream project plus Pydantic under `pydantic-latest`;
- install the upstream project’s locked test environment;
- replace the resolved `pydantic` / `pydantic-core` with the editable checkout; and
- run the upstream’s deterministic, no-secret test suite.

For FastMCP, I would mirror its supported Linux coverage (Python 3.10 and 3.13) and exclude integration/conformance tests that require external credentials or Node tooling. For the MCP Python SDK, I would use its locked unit-test setup across its supported Python versions. This would exercise actual Pydantic-backed models and schema handling rather than only checking that dependencies install.

If that scope or version matrix should be narrower, I’m happy to adjust before opening a PR.

evidence_items.heading: Comment on #12867 by @davidhewitt
Comment on #13071 by @dvzrv
evidence_items.text:
[pydantic/pydantic #13071 Comment by @dvzrv]

No, this would be very resource heavy (requiring a full clone of each upstream repository and custom parsing logic for Cargo.toml files).
Version detection for our thousands of upstreams happens multiple times a day.
zWhen e.g. nvchecker is setup to track upstream tags for new version detection, it uses [`git-ls-remote`](https://man.archlinux.org/man/git-ls-remote.1).
When using PyPI it queries a particular API for a package.

Only during build time, we clone the repository or download a specific tarball to build from (depending on how the PKGBUILD package build script is setup for a given package).

> I'm not against creating pydantic-core specific tags, but I would rather avoid it if not required. This also feels like a more general problem to any library set up as a monorepo.

Yes. That's why projects usually use distinguished tag schemes to target the particular version of the (differing) packages in a monorepo.
See e.g.:

- https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/alpm/alpm/-/tags
- https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/signstar/-/tags

If you only ever use one version for all packages in a monorepo, it would not matter and you could use just a single tag.
However, this is not the case in this repository: pydantic-core is in version 2.46.0 and pydantic in version 2.13.0.

evidence_items.heading: Comment on #13602 by @Viicos
evidence_items.text:
[pydantic/pydantic #13602 Comment by @Viicos]

Hi @psalvaggio,

I've looked at the upstream issue, and this seesm to be an x/y problem. By using a `TypeAdapter` within an existing "validation run" (e.g. validating a model), you are exposing yourself to all kind of issues. Strictness _not_ being forwarded is one of them, but you also loose all information about the current validation run: strictness, but also [validation context](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/concepts/validators/#validation-context), and possibly others.

For your specific case, https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/11154 would presumably solve it, but you are still open to the limitation I mentioned.

Closing as duplicate, happy to reopen if I missed anything.
